top_news.title: Cost-Effective Automated Judging of Natural-Language Mathematical Proofs
top_news.dek: Smaller open-weight models can grade mathematical proofs as effectively as frontier models at a fraction of the cost.
top_news.brief: Researchers found that models like DeepSeek-V4 Flash and Gemma-4 31B match the performance of Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro in grading IMO-level proofs. By using a ground-truth proof and a rubric, these smaller models achieved human-level agreement at up to 100x lower cost.
top_news.image_alt: Chart comparing grading accuracy of small vs large language models

top_news.title: Workers - AI agents can debug Workers with local tracing
top_news.dek: Cloudflare's local development tools now support AI agent-driven debugging via automated OpenTelemetry tracing.
top_news.brief: Wrangler and Vite dev environments now capture structured traces and logs during local Worker invocations. When an AI agent session is detected, the Local Explorer API allows agents to query telemetry, inspect binding states, and verify fixes without requiring deployments.
top_news.image_alt: Cloudflare Workers local development terminal output

top_news.title: Mistral's Shieldstral: 3B open-weights model for multimodal moderation
top_news.dek: Mistral released Shieldstral, a 3B parameter open-weights model designed for multimodal content moderation.
top_news.brief: Shieldstral is a policy-adaptive safety classifier that performs on par with models significantly larger in size. It is designed to handle diverse moderation tasks, such as identifying violence or assessing image safety, without requiring retraining when deployment contexts or safety definitions change.
top_news.image_alt: Shieldstral model architecture diagram showing multimodal input processing

top_news.title: An AI-supervised remote exam went so badly that 58,000 students must retake it
top_news.dek: A large-scale remote exam was invalidated after AI-based proctoring software failed, forcing 58,000 students to retake the test.
top_news.brief: The incident occurred after the AI proctoring system produced anomalous results, including a fivefold increase in top scores, indicating a systemic failure in the automated supervision process.
top_news.image_alt: Abstract representation of a digital exam interface with a warning icon

top_news.title: Cursor Open-Sources Mixture-of-Kittens (MoK): A Deterministic MoE Training Megakernel for GB300 NVL72 Racks
top_news.dek: Cursor open-sourced Mixture-of-Kittens (MoK), a high-performance MoE training kernel optimized for GB300 NVL72 hardware.
top_news.brief: MoK fuses MoE communication and computation into a single deterministic kernel, achieving up to 2.37x higher throughput than existing public baselines. The kernel is designed specifically for Blackwell SM100 or SM103 GPUs, requiring significant hardware infrastructure for deployment.
top_news.image_alt: Performance graph comparing MoK throughput against standard MoE kernels

primary.summary: Cursor Research has open-sourced Mixture-of-Kittens (MoK), the MoE training megakernel behind its Composer models. MoK fuses all mixture-of-experts communication and computation into a single deterministic kernel, and runs up to 2.37x faster than the strongest public baseline on GB300 NVL72 racks. It requires Blackwell SM100 or SM103 GPUs, which puts it out of reach for anyone without NVL72 capacity.
